key_insight: Deep learning models can discover and generate functional internal ribosome entry sites (IRESs) at scale, enabling programmable control of RNA translation. Experimentally validated designs from model-guided generation demonstrate reliable, tunable translation activity for mRNA constructs.
problem_solved: Lack of scalable methods to identify and design functional IRES elements for controlling translation in RNA therapeutics; traditional discovery is slow and low-throughput.
method: Train sequence-to-function deep learning models on high-throughput measurement data linking IRES sequences to translation activity.
Use the trained models to discover novel IRES candidates from large sequence spaces and to generate de novo IRES sequences optimized for desired translation strength.
Validate model predictions with high-throughput functional assays, closing the design–test–learn loop for iterative optimization.
impact: Demonstrates how generative and predictive ML models can accelerate biological part discovery and enable programmable molecular functions, providing a template for AI-driven wet-lab design loops in therapeutics and synthetic biology.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing: data generation → model training → in silico design → high-throughput experimental validation loop.

paper_title: Programmable RNA translation through deep learning-driven IRES discovery and de novo generation
paper_authors: Yanyi Chu, Di Yin, Dan Yu, Guangxue Xu, Junze Zhang
